name: Accounting
title: Bookkeeper
blurb: Accounting is the language every SAP FI/CO project, markets-system P&L and consulting case is written in, and 簿記 certificates are a credential Japanese employers recognise instantly.

chapters.title: Double-entry and journals
chapters.read: A 日商簿記3級 textbook's opening chapters on 仕訳, 勘定科目 and 転記: the five account groups (assets, liabilities, net assets, revenue, expenses), which side each increases on, and how journals post to the general ledger and trial balance (試算表).
chapters.produce: Journalise 25 transactions for a small café's first month in Japanese account names, post them to T-accounts and prepare a balancing trial balance.

quiz.q: The owner starts a business by depositing ¥500,000 of personal cash into it. Which journal entry is correct?
opts: Dr 資本金 (Capital) 500,000 / Cr 現金 (Cash) 500,000
Dr 現金 (Cash) 500,000 / Cr 借入金 (Loans payable) 500,000
Dr 現金 (Cash) 500,000 / Cr 売上 (Sales) 500,000
Dr 現金 (Cash) 500,000 / Cr 資本金 (Capital) 500,000
quiz.ex: Cash (an asset) increases on the debit side; the owner's investment increases capital (net assets), which is a credit.

quiz.q: Which type of account normally carries a credit balance?
opts: Revenue (収益), such as 売上
Assets (資産), such as 売掛金
Assets (資産), such as 現金
Expenses (費用), such as 給料
quiz.ex: Liabilities, net assets and revenue increase on the credit side; assets and expenses increase on the debit side.

quiz.q: Using the three-part method (三分法), the business buys goods for resale for ¥80,000 on credit. Which entry is correct?
opts: Dr 仕入 80,000 / Cr 売掛金 80,000
Dr 仕入 80,000 / Cr 買掛金 80,000
Dr 買掛金 80,000 / Cr 仕入 80,000
Dr 売上 80,000 / Cr 買掛金 80,000
quiz.ex: Purchases of goods are debited to 仕入 (an expense-type account under 三分法) and the amount owed to the supplier is a credit to 買掛金 (accounts payable).

quiz.q: A café starts with zero cash. In its first month: the owner invests ¥1,000,000 cash; it buys equipment for ¥300,000 cash; makes cash sales of ¥50,000; pays rent of ¥80,000 in cash; and borrows ¥200,000 from a bank. What is the cash balance at month end?

A trial balance shows these balances. Debit: Cash 400,000; Receivables 150,000; Equipment 250,000; Expenses 120,000. Credit: Payables 180,000; Sales 340,000; Capital ?. What must the Capital balance be for the trial balance to agree?
quiz.ex: Debits total 920,000. Credits are 180,000 + 340,000 + Capital = 920,000, so Capital = 400,000.

quiz.q: Which error would a trial balance NOT reveal?
opts: A debit of ¥50,000 posted with a credit of ¥5,000
Only the debit side of an entry was posted to the ledger
A credit sale that was never journalised at all
A debit was posted to the ledger twice but the credit only once
quiz.ex: Omitting a whole transaction leaves debits and credits equal, so the trial balance still agrees; the other errors make the totals differ.

chapters.title: The three statements and how they link
chapters.read: An introductory financial accounting text's chapters on the balance sheet (貸借対照表), income statement (損益計算書) and cash flow statement (キャッシュ・フロー計算書), focusing on how net income flows to retained earnings and how the indirect method reconciles profit to operating cash flow.
chapters.produce: Take one Japanese listed company's 決算短信 summary figures and draw a one-page diagram showing how net income, retained earnings, cash and the three cash flow sections connect, with the actual numbers.

quiz.q: Net income for the year is carried into which balance sheet item?
opts: Accounts payable
Cash and deposits
Share capital (資本金)
Retained earnings (繰越利益剰余金) within net assets
quiz.ex: Profit belongs to the owners and accumulates in retained earnings; this is the main link between the income statement and the balance sheet.

quiz.q: In the indirect method of preparing the cash flow statement, why is depreciation added back to net income?
opts: It is a financing activity
It is a cash inflow from selling fixed assets
It reduced profit but involved no cash payment in the period
It increases the book value of fixed assets
quiz.ex: Depreciation is a non-cash expense: the cash left when the asset was bought, so it is added back to convert profit to operating cash flow.

quiz.q: A company reports: revenue ¥5,000,000; cost of sales ¥3,000,000; selling, general and administrative expenses ¥1,200,000; interest expense ¥100,000. What is its operating income (営業利益)?
quiz.ex: Operating income = 5,000,000 − 3,000,000 − 1,200,000 = 800,000. Interest expense is non-operating and comes after operating income.

quiz.q: Using the indirect method: net income ¥600,000; depreciation ¥150,000; accounts receivable increased by ¥80,000; inventory decreased by ¥30,000; accounts payable increased by ¥40,000. What is cash flow from operating activities?
quiz.ex: 600,000 + 150,000 − 80,000 + 30,000 + 40,000 = 740,000. An increase in a current asset uses cash; an increase in a current liability provides cash.

quiz.q: A company buys a delivery truck for cash. In which section of the cash flow statement does the payment appear?
opts: Investing activities
Operating activities
It does not appear because the truck is an asset
Financing activities
quiz.ex: Purchases and sales of fixed assets are investing cash flows.

quiz.q: Retained earnings at the start of the year were ¥2,000,000. Net income was ¥700,000 and dividends paid were ¥300,000. What are retained earnings at year end?

chapters.title: Accruals and deferrals
chapters.read: A 簿記3級 textbook's chapter on 経過勘定 (前払費用, 未払費用, 前受収益, 未収収益) and 再振替仕訳, with the accrual principle that revenue and expenses belong to the period they relate to, not the period cash moves.
chapters.produce: For ten realistic year-end situations (insurance, rent, interest, wages) write the adjusting entry and the following year's reversing entry, with month-count working shown.

quiz.q: On 1 December the company paid ¥240,000 for 12 months of insurance and debited 保険料. The year ends on 31 March. What amount should be shown as prepaid insurance (前払保険料) at year end?
quiz.ex: Monthly cost 20,000. December to March (4 months) is this year's expense; April to November (8 months) is prepaid: 8 × 20,000 = 160,000.

quiz.q: On 1 January the company borrowed ¥1,000,000 at 3% per year, with all interest payable at repayment on 31 December. The year ends on 31 March. How much accrued interest (未払利息) should be recorded at year end?
quiz.ex: 1,000,000 × 3% × 3/12 = 7,500 for January to March.

quiz.q: At year end, rent received in advance for the next accounting period is shown on the balance sheet as:
opts: Revenue of the current year
未収収益 (accrued revenue), an asset
前受収益 (unearned revenue), a liability
前払費用 (prepaid expense), an asset
quiz.ex: Cash received for a service not yet provided is an obligation to provide it, so it is deferred as a liability.

quiz.q: Wages of ¥30,000 for the last days of March are unpaid at the 31 March year end. Which adjusting entry is correct?
opts: Dr 給料 30,000 / Cr 未払給料 30,000
Dr 未払給料 30,000 / Cr 給料 30,000
Dr 前払給料 30,000 / Cr 給料 30,000
quiz.ex: The expense belongs to this year so 給料 is debited; the unpaid amount is a liability, 未払給料 (an accrued expense).

quiz.q: What is the purpose of the reversing entry (再振替仕訳) made on the first day of the new year?
opts: To record depreciation for the new year
To cancel last year's accrual or deferral so that the next cash payment or receipt can be recorded in the normal way
To correct errors found in last year's ledger
To close revenue and expense accounts to capital
quiz.ex: Reversing the adjustment moves the deferred or accrued amount back into the revenue or expense account, so the year's total ends up correct when cash moves.

quiz.q: On 1 August the company received ¥360,000 of rent covering August to the following July and credited 受取家賃. The year ends on 31 March. How much rent revenue belongs to the current year?
quiz.ex: Monthly rent 30,000. August to March is 8 months: 8 × 30,000 = 240,000. The remaining 120,000 is 前受家賃.

chapters.title: Depreciation
chapters.read: A 簿記3級/2級 textbook's chapters on 有形固定資産 and 減価償却: straight-line (定額法) and declining-balance (定率法) methods, monthly pro-rating for mid-year purchases, the indirect method with 減価償却累計額, and gains and losses on disposal.
chapters.produce: Build a spreadsheet depreciation schedule for three assets (one bought mid-year, one on declining balance, one sold in year three) that outputs annual expense, accumulated depreciation, book value and the disposal entry.

quiz.q: Equipment costing ¥1,200,000 is bought on the first day of the accounting year. Useful life 5 years, residual value zero, straight-line method. What is the annual depreciation expense?
A machine costing ¥600,000 is bought on 1 October. Useful life 6 years, residual value zero, straight-line, depreciated monthly. The year ends on 31 March. What is depreciation for the first year?
quiz.ex: Annual depreciation is 600,000 ÷ 6 = 100,000. October to March is 6 months: 100,000 × 6/12 = 50,000.

quiz.q: An asset costing ¥1,000,000 is depreciated using the declining-balance method (定率法) at a rate of 40% per year. What is the depreciation expense in year 2?
Under the indirect method (間接法) of recording depreciation, which entry is correct?
opts: Dr 減価償却費 / Cr 備品
Dr 減価償却累計額 / Cr 減価償却費
Dr 減価償却費 / Cr 減価償却累計額
Dr 備品 / Cr 減価償却累計額
quiz.ex: The indirect method keeps the asset at cost and builds up the contra-asset 減価償却累計額; crediting the asset account directly is the direct method.

quiz.q: Equipment with cost ¥800,000 and accumulated depreciation ¥500,000 is sold for ¥250,000 cash. What is the loss on sale (固定資産売却損)?
Why is land (土地) not depreciated?
opts: It is always shown at market value instead
It is too expensive to depreciate
It is a current asset
It does not wear out or get used up, so it has no finite useful life
quiz.ex: Depreciation spreads cost over the period an asset is used up; land is not consumed, so its cost is not spread.

chapters.title: Inventory: FIFO and weighted average
chapters.read: A 簿記3級/2級 textbook's chapters on 商品有高帳 and 売上原価: first-in first-out (先入先出法), moving average (移動平均法) and periodic weighted average (総平均法), plus the 三分法 closing entries that compute cost of sales.
chapters.produce: Fill in a 商品有高帳 (stock ledger) for one month of purchases and sales twice, once with FIFO and once with moving average, and reconcile COGS + ending inventory to goods available for sale.

quiz.q:
Use this data for one month:
Opening: 100 units @ ¥200
Purchase 1: 300 units @ ¥220
Sale 1: 250 units
Purchase 2: 200 units @ ¥250
Sale 2: 200 units
Using FIFO, what is total cost of goods sold for the month?

Same data:
Opening: 100 units @ ¥200
Purchase 1: 300 units @ ¥220
Sale 1: 250 units
Purchase 2: 200 units @ ¥250
Sale 2: 200 units
Using FIFO, what is the value of ending inventory?
quiz.ex: 150 units remain, all from Purchase 2: 150 × 250 = 37,500. Check: goods available 136,000 − COGS 98,500 = 37,500.

quiz.q:
Same data:
Opening: 100 units @ ¥200
Purchase 1: 300 units @ ¥220
Sale 1: 250 units
Purchase 2: 200 units @ ¥250
Sale 2: 200 units
Using the moving average method (移動平均法), what is total cost of goods sold?
Opening inventory 200 units @ ¥300; purchases during the year 300 units @ ¥350; 400 units sold. Using the periodic weighted average method (総平均法), what is cost of goods sold?
When purchase prices are rising, how does FIFO compare with the weighted average method?
opts: FIFO gives higher cost of goods sold
FIFO gives higher ending inventory and higher gross profit
FIFO gives lower ending inventory and lower gross profit
Both methods always give the same profit
quiz.ex: FIFO sends the older, cheaper costs to COGS and leaves the newer, dearer costs in inventory, so COGS is lower and profit higher.

quiz.q: Under 三分法, which pair of year-end entries turns the 仕入 account into cost of goods sold?
opts: Dr 仕入 / Cr 売上, then Dr 繰越商品 / Cr 売上
Dr 繰越商品 / Cr 仕入 (opening stock), then Dr 仕入 / Cr 繰越商品 (closing stock)
Dr 売上 / Cr 仕入, then Dr 仕入 / Cr 繰越商品
Dr 仕入 / Cr 繰越商品 (opening stock), then Dr 繰越商品 / Cr 仕入 (closing stock)
quiz.ex: Adding opening inventory to purchases and removing closing inventory leaves 仕入 equal to opening + purchases − closing = COGS (しーくりくりしー).

chapters.title: Receivables, payables, bad debts and provisions
chapters.read: A 簿記3級/2級 textbook's chapters on 売掛金・買掛金, 手形 and 貸倒引当金 (差額補充法), followed by an intermediate text's section on provisions (引当金, IAS 37 recognition criteria) such as bonus and warranty provisions.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page 'receivables to bad debt' walkthrough with entries for a credit sale, a note received, a write-off of a prior-year and a current-year debt, and the year-end allowance top-up.

quiz.q: At year end, accounts receivable total ¥2,000,000. The company provides for bad debts at 2% using the 差額補充法 (top-up method). The allowance (貸倒引当金) currently has a balance of ¥15,000. What is the bad debt provision expense (貸倒引当金繰入) for the year?
A receivable of ¥30,000 that arose in the previous year becomes uncollectible. The allowance for bad debts has a balance of ¥50,000. Which entry is correct?
opts: Dr 貸倒損失 30,000 / Cr 貸倒引当金 30,000
Dr 貸倒引当金 30,000 / Cr 貸倒損失 30,000
Dr 貸倒引当金 30,000 / Cr 売掛金 30,000
Dr 売掛金 30,000 / Cr 貸倒引当金 30,000
quiz.ex: The allowance was created last year for exactly this kind of loss, so it is used up and the receivable is removed.

quiz.q: A prior-year receivable of ¥80,000 is written off. The allowance for bad debts has a balance of only ¥50,000. How much must be recognised as 貸倒損失 (bad debt loss)?
quiz.ex: The allowance absorbs 50,000; the remaining 80,000 − 50,000 = 30,000 is charged to 貸倒損失.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a condition for recognising a provision under IFRS (IAS 37)?
opts: An outflow of resources is probable
The amount can be estimated reliably
The exact amount of the future payment must be known
There is a present obligation arising from a past event
quiz.ex: A provision is a liability of uncertain timing or amount; it needs a reliable estimate, not an exact figure.

quiz.q: Employees will be paid a bonus of ¥1,200,000 in June covering their work from December to May. The year ends on 31 March. What bonus provision (賞与引当金) should be recognised at year end?
quiz.ex: December to March is 4 of the 6 months: 1,200,000 × 4/6 = 800,000.

quiz.q: A customer settles an existing ¥100,000 account receivable by giving the company a promissory note. Which entry is correct?
opts: Dr 売掛金 100,000 / Cr 受取手形 100,000
Dr 支払手形 100,000 / Cr 売掛金 100,000
Dr 受取手形 100,000 / Cr 売上 100,000
Dr 受取手形 100,000 / Cr 売掛金 100,000
quiz.ex: One receivable (売掛金) is swapped for another (受取手形, notes receivable); no new sale occurs.

chapters.title: 簿記3級 closing and the 精算表
chapters.read: A 簿記3級 textbook's 決算 chapters: the standard 決算整理事項 (現金過不足, 貯蔵品, 売上原価, 貸倒引当金, 減価償却, 経過勘定), the 8-column 精算表, and closing entries through the 損益 account to 繰越利益剰余金. Then do several timed past-style 第3問 problems.
chapters.produce: Complete three full 精算表 problems from a 簿記3級 problem book under exam timing, and keep an error log of every mistake by type.

quiz.q: On an 8-column 精算表, an adjusted expense balance is extended into which column?
opts: 損益計算書 credit column
損益計算書 debit column
貸借対照表 credit column
貸借対照表 debit column
quiz.ex: Expenses are debit balances that belong in the income statement, so they go to the P&L debit column.

quiz.q:
Trial balance and adjustments:
Sales 3,000,000; 仕入 1,800,000; 繰越商品 (opening) 200,000; closing inventory 250,000
Salaries paid 600,000; unpaid salaries at year end 30,000
Depreciation for the year 100,000
Rent paid 240,000, of which 60,000 relates to next year
What is net income for the year?
Opening merchandise ¥150,000, purchases ¥2,400,000, closing merchandise ¥180,000. What is cost of goods sold (売上原価)?
During the year a cash shortage of ¥3,000 was debited to 現金過不足. At year end the cause is still unknown. Which closing entry is correct?
opts: Dr 雑損 3,000 / Cr 現金 3,000
Dr 雑損 3,000 / Cr 現金過不足 3,000
Dr 現金 3,000 / Cr 現金過不足 3,000
Dr 現金過不足 3,000 / Cr 雑益 3,000
quiz.ex: The unexplained shortage becomes a miscellaneous loss (雑損), clearing the debit in 現金過不足. Cash was already corrected when the shortage was found.

quiz.q: During the year postage stamps costing ¥12,000 were bought and debited to 通信費. At year end ¥4,000 of stamps are unused and are moved to 貯蔵品. What is 通信費 for the year?
quiz.ex: Dr 貯蔵品 4,000 / Cr 通信費 4,000, leaving 12,000 − 4,000 = 8,000 as expense.

quiz.q: After the closing entries are posted, which accounts have a zero balance?
opts: All asset accounts
Every account in the ledger
All revenue and expense accounts
All liability accounts
quiz.ex: Revenues and expenses are closed to the 損益 account and then to 繰越利益剰余金; balance sheet accounts carry forward.

chapters.title: Consolidated accounts basics (簿記2級)
chapters.read: A 簿記2級 商業簿記 textbook's 連結会計 chapters: 投資と資本の相殺消去, のれん, 非支配株主持分, elimination of intra-group balances and 未実現利益, plus the idea of control versus significant influence (持分法).
chapters.produce: Prepare a consolidation worksheet for a parent and an 80% subsidiary at acquisition and one year later, showing goodwill, NCI, intra-group eliminations and the consolidated balance sheet.

quiz.q: Parent P pays ¥1,000,000 for 80% of S. At that date S's net assets at fair value are ¥1,100,000 (capital 800,000 + retained earnings 300,000). What goodwill (のれん) arises?
Same acquisition: P buys 80% of S, whose net assets are ¥1,100,000. What is the non-controlling interest (非支配株主持分) at acquisition, measured at its share of net assets?
Parent P sold goods to subsidiary S for ¥500,000, at a profit of 20% of the selling price. At year end S still holds 30% of these goods. How much unrealised profit (未実現利益) must be eliminated?
quiz.ex: Goods still held: 500,000 × 30% = 150,000. Profit included: 150,000 × 20% = 30,000.

quiz.q: At year end P has a ¥200,000 receivable from its subsidiary S, and S has the matching payable. Which consolidation entry eliminates them?
opts: Dr 買掛金 200,000 / Cr 売掛金 200,000
Dr のれん 200,000 / Cr 売掛金 200,000
Dr 売掛金 200,000 / Cr 買掛金 200,000
Dr 売上 200,000 / Cr 売上原価 200,000
quiz.ex: The group cannot owe itself money, so the payable (debit to remove) and receivable (credit to remove) cancel out.

quiz.q: Under J-GAAP, how is goodwill arising on consolidation treated after acquisition?
opts: It is expensed in full on the acquisition date
It is amortised over a period of up to 20 years
It is never amortised and only tested for impairment
It is added to non-controlling interest
quiz.ex: J-GAAP requires systematic amortisation within 20 years (with impairment testing as needed); IFRS does not amortise goodwill.

quiz.q: Company A holds 30% of Company B's voting shares and has significant influence but not control. How does A normally account for B in its consolidated statements?
opts: Full line-by-line consolidation
As a subsidiary with 70% non-controlling interest
Equity method (持分法)
It is ignored until B pays a dividend
quiz.ex: Significant influence without control makes B an affiliate (関連会社), accounted for by the equity method.

chapters.title: Tax-effect accounting (税効果会計)
chapters.read: A 簿記2級 textbook's 税効果会計 chapter: temporary versus permanent differences, 繰延税金資産 and 繰延税金負債, 法人税等調整額, and the treatment of その他有価証券評価差額金.
chapters.produce: For five temporary differences (excess bad debt provision, excess depreciation, securities revaluation, and two of your choice) write the origination and reversal entries and show how reported tax expense comes to the statutory rate times pre-tax profit.

quiz.q: Accounting depreciation is ¥500,000 but only ¥300,000 is deductible for tax this year (the rest will be deductible later). The effective tax rate is 30%. What deferred tax asset (繰延税金資産) arises?
Pre-tax profit is ¥1,000,000. Current tax payable (法人税等) is ¥360,000. A deferred tax asset of ¥60,000 is recognised this year. What is net income?
quiz.ex: 法人税等調整額 is a credit (reduction of tax expense) of 60,000. Total tax = 360,000 − 60,000 = 300,000. Net income = 1,000,000 − 300,000 = 700,000.

quiz.q: Which item creates a temporary difference rather than a permanent one?
opts: Fines and penalties that are never deductible
Entertainment expenses that are never deductible (交際費)
Dividends received that are excluded from taxable income
Bad debt provision in excess of the tax-deductible limit (貸倒引当金繰入限度超過額)
quiz.ex: An excess provision becomes deductible later when the debt is actually written off, so the difference reverses. The others never reverse.

quiz.q: Which entry records the recognition of a deferred tax asset of ¥60,000?
opts: Dr 法人税等調整額 60,000 / Cr 繰延税金資産 60,000
Dr 繰延税金負債 60,000 / Cr 法人税等調整額 60,000
Dr 繰延税金資産 60,000 / Cr 法人税等調整額 60,000
Dr 法人税等 60,000 / Cr 未払法人税等 60,000
quiz.ex: The asset is debited and the credit to 法人税等調整額 reduces total tax expense in the P&L.

quiz.q: A deferred tax asset should be recognised only to the extent that:
opts: Shareholders approve it at the annual general meeting
Tax rates are expected to rise
The company has enough cash to pay this year's tax
Sufficient future taxable income is expected to absorb the deductible difference
quiz.ex: A future deduction only saves tax if there will be taxable profit to deduct it from; this is the recoverability test.

quiz.q: その他有価証券 (available-for-sale securities) bought for ¥1,000,000 are worth ¥1,100,000 at year end. The company uses the 全部純資産直入法 and a 30% tax rate. What amount is recorded as その他有価証券評価差額金 in net assets?
quiz.ex: Gain 100,000. Deferred tax liability 100,000 × 30% = 30,000. Net of tax to net assets: 100,000 − 30,000 = 70,000.

chapters.title: Industrial bookkeeping basics (工業簿記)
chapters.read: A 簿記2級 工業簿記 textbook's early chapters: 材料費・労務費・経費, direct versus indirect costs, 製造間接費 and predetermined overhead rates with 配賦差異, the flow from 仕掛品 to 製品, and an introduction to 総合原価計算 with equivalent units.
chapters.produce: Draw the full 工業簿記 account flow (材料 → 仕掛品 → 製品 → 売上原価, with 製造間接費) for a small furniture maker and fill in one month of numbers that tie to a 製造原価報告書.

quiz.q: Factory building rent belongs to which cost element (原価要素)?
opts: 経費 (other manufacturing expenses)
労務費 (labour)
販売費 (selling expense)
材料費 (materials)
quiz.ex: Costs that are neither materials nor labour, like factory rent, utilities and depreciation, are 経費.

quiz.q: Materials: opening stock ¥200,000, purchases ¥1,500,000, closing stock ¥300,000. What is the cost of materials consumed (材料費)?
Opening work in process ¥300,000; total manufacturing costs this period ¥2,500,000; closing work in process ¥400,000. What is the cost of goods manufactured (当期製品製造原価)?
Overhead is applied at a predetermined rate of ¥1,200 per machine hour. Actual machine hours were 900 and actual overhead was ¥1,150,000. By how much was overhead under-applied (the 製造間接費配賦差異)?
quiz.ex: Applied = 900 × 1,200 = 1,080,000. Actual 1,150,000 − 1,080,000 = 70,000 under-applied (an unfavourable difference).

quiz.q: A furniture maker incurs these costs. Which is an indirect manufacturing cost (製造間接費)?
opts: Wages of a worker who assembles a specific order
Outside processing (外注加工賃) for a specific order
Wood used in a specific chair
The salary of the factory supervisor
quiz.ex: The supervisor's salary benefits all products and cannot be traced to one, so it is overhead; the others are traceable direct costs.

quiz.q: A process starts 1,000 units with no opening work in process. 800 units are completed; 200 units remain 50% complete for conversion. Conversion costs for the period are ¥900,000. What conversion cost is assigned to closing work in process?

chapters.title: J-GAAP vs IFRS and revenue recognition
chapters.read: An overview from a Big Four firm's or the ASBJ's comparison material on J-GAAP versus IFRS (goodwill, extraordinary items, presentation), then the five-step model of IFRS 15 and Japan's 収益認識に関する会計基準, including performance obligations and principal versus agent.
chapters.produce: Write a one-page comparison table of the ten J-GAAP vs IFRS differences you would most likely meet on an SAP FI project, and work through three five-step revenue examples (bundle, subscription, agent sale).

quiz.q: In the five-step revenue recognition model, what is step 3?
opts: Determine the transaction price
Identify the performance obligations
Recognise revenue when a performance obligation is satisfied
Allocate the transaction price to performance obligations
quiz.ex: The order is: identify the contract, identify performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate it, recognise revenue.

quiz.q: A carrier sells a phone with a 24-month service plan for a total of ¥120,000. Stand-alone selling prices are: phone ¥90,000, service ¥60,000. How much of the transaction price is allocated to the phone?
quiz.ex: Allocate in proportion to stand-alone prices: 120,000 × 90,000 / 150,000 = 72,000.

quiz.q: In the same deal, ¥48,000 is allocated to the 24-month service, which starts on 1 April and is provided evenly. The year ends on 31 March. How much service revenue is recognised in the first year?
quiz.ex: Service is satisfied over time: 48,000 × 12/24 = 24,000.

quiz.q: Which statement describes a real difference between J-GAAP and IFRS?
opts: IFRS does not require a balance sheet
J-GAAP amortises goodwill; IFRS does not amortise it but tests it for impairment
IFRS prohibits consolidated financial statements
J-GAAP does not use the accrual basis
quiz.ex: Goodwill amortisation is one of the best-known differences; the other options are false for both frameworks.

quiz.q: How does Japan's revenue recognition standard (収益認識に関する会計基準) relate to IFRS 15?
opts: It applies only to banks and insurers
It is built on the same five-step model as IFRS 15
It requires revenue to be recognised when a contract is signed
It recognises revenue only when cash is received
quiz.ex: The ASBJ based the Japanese standard on IFRS 15's core principle and five steps, with some additional practical expedients.

quiz.q: A department store sells a supplier's goods on a consignment-style basis (消化仕入) and acts as an agent. A customer pays ¥10,000; the store passes ¥8,000 to the supplier. How much revenue does the store recognise?
quiz.ex: An agent recognises only its net commission: 10,000 − 8,000 = 2,000.

chapters.title: Japanese specifics: 消費税, インボイス, 電子帳簿保存法
chapters.read: A 簿記3級/2級 textbook's 消費税 (税抜方式) section with 仮払消費税・仮受消費税・未払消費税, then the National Tax Agency's plain-language guides to the qualified invoice system (インボイス制度) and the electronic record-keeping law (電子帳簿保存法), focusing on the core rules.
chapters.produce: Journalise a month of sales and purchases for a café with mixed 8% and 10% items using the tax-excluded method, compute the consumption tax payable, and list which fields a 適格請求書 must contain.

quiz.q: Using the tax-excluded method (税抜方式), a company buys goods for ¥200,000 plus 10% consumption tax and sells them for ¥350,000 plus 10% consumption tax. What consumption tax payable (未払消費税) is recorded at year end?
Using the tax-excluded method, goods costing ¥100,000 plus 10% consumption tax are bought on credit. Which entry is correct?
opts: Dr 仕入 100,000 and 仮払消費税 10,000 / Cr 買掛金 110,000
Dr 仕入 100,000 / Cr 買掛金 100,000 and 仮払消費税 10,000
Dr 仕入 100,000 and 仮受消費税 10,000 / Cr 買掛金 110,000
quiz.ex: Tax paid on purchases is held in 仮払消費税 (an asset) rather than in the cost; the supplier is owed the tax-inclusive 110,000.

quiz.q: Under the qualified invoice system (インボイス制度), what does a buyer in principle need in order to claim an input tax credit (仕入税額控除)?
opts: A qualified invoice (適格請求書) from a registered issuer, showing its registration number
A bank statement showing the payment
Any till receipt showing the total paid
A signed purchase contract without tax details
quiz.ex: In principle the input tax credit depends on keeping a 適格請求書 issued by a 適格請求書発行事業者, which carries a registration number and tax by rate.

quiz.q: A supermarket's monthly sales (excluding tax) are ¥500,000 of food taxed at the reduced 8% rate and ¥200,000 of household goods taxed at 10%. What is the output consumption tax (仮受消費税) for the month?
Under 電子帳簿保存法, a supplier sends an invoice only as a PDF by email (電子取引). What is the basic storage rule?
opts: Keep the electronic data; printing it out and keeping only the paper copy does not meet the requirement
Print it and delete the PDF
Forward it to the tax office within 7 days
Keep nothing, because emailed invoices are not records
quiz.ex: Data received electronically must be kept as electronic data meeting the law's integrity and retrieval requirements.

quiz.q: Under the tax-excluded method, how does consumption tax affect the income statement?
opts: The net amount payable is expensed as 租税公課
It is not revenue or expense; it sits in 仮受消費税 and 仮払消費税 and the net is settled with the tax office
Input tax is added to cost of goods sold
Output tax is recorded as sales revenue
quiz.ex: With 税抜方式 the business only collects and passes on the tax; expensing the net as 租税公課 is the tax-inclusive method.

boss.q: A machine costing ¥2,400,000 was bought on 1 July of Year 1. Straight-line, 8-year life, zero residual, depreciated monthly. The year ends on 31 March. It is sold on 30 September of Year 3 for ¥1,700,000. What is the loss on sale?

The allowance for bad debts started the year at ¥70,000. During the year a prior-year receivable of ¥50,000 was written off against it. Year-end receivables are ¥3,500,000 and the company provides 2% using the top-up method. What is 貸倒引当金繰入 for the year?

Indirect method data: net income ¥900,000; depreciation ¥200,000; loss on sale of equipment ¥25,000; receivables up ¥120,000; inventory up ¥60,000; payables down ¥40,000; accrued expenses up ¥15,000. What is operating cash flow?
boss.ex: 900,000 + 200,000 + 25,000 − 120,000 − 60,000 − 40,000 + 15,000 = 920,000. The loss is added back because the cash proceeds belong in investing.

boss.q: P bought 60% of S for ¥2,000,000 when S had capital ¥2,500,000 and retained earnings ¥500,000 (book value equals fair value). In the next year S earned net income of ¥400,000 and paid no dividends. What is non-controlling interest at the end of that year?

Pre-tax profit ¥2,000,000; tax rate 30%. Non-deductible entertainment expenses (permanent) ¥100,000. Excess bad debt provision (temporary, arising this year) ¥200,000. Using tax-effect accounting, what is net income?
boss.ex: Taxable income 2,300,000 → current tax 690,000. DTA 200,000 × 30% = 60,000 reduces tax expense to 630,000. Net income = 2,000,000 − 630,000 = 1,370,000.

boss.q: Book inventory is 500 units at a cost of ¥400. A count finds 480 units. The net selling value is ¥360 per unit. What is the inventory valuation loss (商品評価損), separate from the shortage loss (棚卸減耗損)?
boss.ex: Shortage: 20 × 400 = 8,000 (棚卸減耗損). Valuation loss on units actually held: 480 × (400 − 360) = 19,200.

boss.q: A gym sells a one-year membership for ¥120,000 paid in advance on 1 January. Its year ends on 31 March. How should this appear in the year-end accounts?
opts: Revenue ¥30,000 and a receivable of ¥90,000
Revenue ¥120,000 because the cash has been received
No revenue until the membership year ends
Revenue ¥30,000 and a contract liability (契約負債) of ¥90,000
boss.ex: The service is satisfied over time; 3 of 12 months have passed, so 30,000 is earned and 90,000 is still owed as service.

boss.q: Process costing, average method. Opening WIP 200 units (50% converted) with conversion cost ¥90,000. Units started 1,800. Units completed 1,600. Closing WIP 400 units, 25% converted. Conversion costs added this period ¥1,610,000. What conversion cost is assigned to the completed units?
boss.ex: Equivalent units = 1,600 + 400 × 25% = 1,700. Total conversion cost 90,000 + 1,610,000 = 1,700,000, so ¥1,000 per unit. Completed 1,600 × 1,000 = 1,600,000.

boss.q: Tax-excluded method, 10% rate on everything. Sales (excl. tax) ¥6,000,000; purchases of goods (excl. tax) ¥3,500,000; equipment bought (excl. tax) ¥1,000,000; interim consumption tax already paid (中間納付) ¥50,000. What 未払消費税 is recorded at year end?
boss.ex: Output 600,000 − input (350,000 + 100,000) = 150,000 owed for the year, less 50,000 already paid = 100,000.

boss.q: Which statement about income statement presentation is correct?
opts: J-GAAP shows 特別利益 and 特別損失, while IFRS prohibits presenting items as 'extraordinary'
J-GAAP prohibits extraordinary items, while IFRS requires them
Both J-GAAP and IFRS prohibit any separate line for unusual items
IFRS requires extraordinary items to be shown separately
boss.ex: The Japanese P&L has 経常利益 then 特別利益・特別損失; IFRS does not allow any item to be labelled extraordinary.
